title: Windows 11 preview update results in invalid certificate error - timezone change
creator: evilspoons
content:
Hi there.

I'm in Alberta, where we have recently changed timezones. Note that the CLOCK has not changed yet, as we are still before the date in November when we would "fall back". We were UTC-6 summer and UTC-7 winter. Windows called this "Mountain Time (USA and Canada), but now the "Mountain Time (Alberta)" timezone is in Windows after the 2026-09 Preview Update (KB5124010) (26300.9550).

When connecting to Shaw.ca's IMAP servers, the certificates that were valid prior to the Windows update are now reported as invalid. This has been confirmed across two separate PCs with different email accounts. The data for the certificate LOOKS valid (see screenshot) and is the same before and after the timezone change.

The failure occurred on the latest ESR release of Thunderbird, as well as 156.0 and 157.0 non-ESR.

Thanks :)

content:

title: Problemi di ricezione mail
creator: omega62
content:
Buongiorno, Premetto che faccio gestire a Thunderbird 5 account di posta, 2 di libero.it, 1 con yahoo.com, 1 con gmail.com e 1 pec con le poste, Thunderbird ha sempre funzionato bene ma da qualche settimana non scarica sempre la posta dal server di libero.it, invece gli altri account funzionano benissimo.

Succede che durante la giornata prevalentemente non scarica in automatico la posta dal server di libero.it, se forzo la richiesta manualmente sembra che si colleghi al server ma non preleva nessuna mail nonostante ci siano dei messaggi non scaricati, poi andando a vedere la posta in arrivo 1 o 2 volte al giorno mi ritrovo con qualche messaggio nuovo che ha prelevato dal server (non tutti) . In questi giorni invece appena apro il programma o forzo manualmente la richiesta di mail si apre una finestra che dice di inserire la pass del miei account di libero, le inserisco ma mi dice che sono errate nonostante siano corrette. Cosa posso fare per risolvere il problema? Non vorrei cancellare e reistallare il programma perchè ho delle date in agenda e delle mail e sottocartelle che mi servono.

title: multiple problems with thunderbird handling gmail accounts
creator: joel.kovarsky
content: For the last few months (several updates to Thunderbird) we are having a terrible time with our gmail accounts in Thunderbird. I am not that tech savvy, but so far nothing has worked (including a Thunderbird uninstall and reinstall). All server settings appear fine, and set to OAuth. We get random extra folders, random deleted folders, trouble with getting copies to sent mail (subscribe OK; have to go to Google's webmail site). This ONLY appears to be a problem with our iMac (M1 chip), and is not occurring with our Macbook Air (M2 chip). I've attempted a few other suggestions thrown up online, but I'm reluctant to tamper too much, and we are increasingly forced to rely on the Google webmail site for adequate function while on the iMac (again, MacBook Air is mostly OK).

I tried all the suggestions I found on the internet, but none of them solved it:

  • Add the account again, then delete again
  • In Thunderbird Settings - Privacy and Security - Saved Passwords: delete anything with that name
  • In Account Settings - Outgoing Server: delete anything with that name
  • Calendar: delete anything with that name

Finally, one more thing did it:

  • Address book: delete anything with that name;
  • even delete address book with no name. Aha! It was this last step that did it.

content:
I had my dad on Thunderbird, and migrated him to Evolution, after your horrible failure. I only wish there was a Mac version, I'm stuck on Thunderbird on my Macs. There are a lot of authors now coming to Linux, that know nothing about it, and don't know how to use apt, so they try that sandboxed shit, not understanding that's why a lot of people are abandoning Windows and Mac in the first place. What you did is complete BS, and unlike some of those newer people moving to Linux, you can't blame ignorance, because you are not new.

title: Norton blocks Thunderbird email due to "expired certificate"
creator: zizumara
content:
I have Thunderbird installed on Windows 11 along with Norton 360. Today, my connection to the AT&T e-mail server suddenly disconnected and I immediately got a pop-up notification that Norton detected a problem with a security certificate. When I inspected the details, it indicated that the certificate for inbound.att.net had expired (the range of valid dates on the certificate actually listed the current date as the last valid date). After several infuriating calls with AT&T support and Norton support, I figured out that simply disabling Norton e-mail protection allowed me to access my e-mail account.

Multiple web searches on similar issues suggested that since Thunderbird has its own certificate storage, fixing the problem involves locating the Norton certificate file and importing it using Thunderbird's certificate manager. Unfortunately, that solution appears to be applicable for first-time Thunderbird installation, and I when I tried it I was informed that the certificate was already installed. Another web search suggested that I should go to the Authorities tab and remove the entry for "Norton Email Protection". Unfortunately, the entry that I found was for "Norton Web/Mail Shield", which according to at least one source is not the same thing, so I am afraid to remove it.

So my question is has anyone else encountered this same problem, and is the correct approach to remove the Norton Web/Mail Shield authority before importing Norton's certificate file?

title: Custom tags disappearing in all folders after switching views (since Sept 28, 2026)
creator: ig2
content:
Dear Thunderbird Support Team,

I am writing to report an issue with custom message tags in Thunderbird that started occurring around September 28, 2026 (likely following a recent update).

Issue Description: The problem applies to all folders (Inbox, Sent, custom subfolders, etc.) and is strictly isolated to user-created (custom) tags.

When I apply a custom tag to any email, the tag visually attaches to the message. However, as soon as I switch to another folder in the folder pane and then return to the original folder, the custom tag disappears completely.

Key Observations:

No Relation to Filters: This issue happens with regular emails in any folder, with no filters involved.

Custom Tags vs. Default Tags: This affects only custom tags created by the user. Default built-in tags (e.g., Important, Work, To Do) save correctly and persist after switching folders.

Timeline: All custom tags assigned before September 28, 2026, are still preserved correctly on older emails. The issue affects any new attempt to set a custom tag after this date.

Steps to Reproduce:

Select any email in any folder.

Apply a user-created (custom) tag to the email.

Observe that the tag is visually assigned.

Click on any other folder to switch views.

Return to the original folder — the applied custom tag is gone.

Could you please assist in resolving this issue or suggest a fix/workaround? Custom tags are essential for our daily email management.

Thank you for your help and support.

Best regards,

title: How can I restore missing Local Folders and emails after Thunderbird re-install?
creator: marek74aw
content:
I've been using Thunderbird for several years, but I still don't quite understand how it works. A week ago or so I was unable to add attachments to email and it was suggested to me that I should reinstall Thunderbird, and the claim was made that I would lose neither my email nor the settings. So I did reinstall Thunderbird and found out that all my Local Folders were gone and that I had to configure all my email accounts from scratch, which I did.

Since I regularly back up my home directory using the Ubuntu Backups app, I thought I could restore my Thunderbird data from a recent back-up. Following some advice I'd found on the internet, I restored the ~/.thunderbird directory from a recent backup and saved it at the desktop. Then I replaced the current ~/.thunderbird directory with the one restored from the back-up (cp -r ~/Desktop/.thunderbird/ ~/). When I re-launched Thunderbird, I noticed the following: (1) All the Local Folders that I had created in 2024 and before were restored, but not the more recent ones (i.e, the ones created in 2025 and 2026). (2) The restored Local Folders did not contain any emails dated after early September 2024, which I think is the time when I upgraded Ubuntu 22.04 to Ubuntu 24.04. Looking at the restored profile directory (~/Desktop/.thunderbird/cvb2eouj.default-release/Mail/Local\ Folders), I see that the missing Local Folders are not there, which makes me believe that the problem happened at the stage of making a back-up of my home directory rather than during the restoration process. Is it possible that the location of Thunderbird data moved from ~/.thunderbird elsewhere at the time when the transition to the snap version of Thunderbird took place in Ubuntu 24.04? If so, what is the new location? Knowing the names of some of the missing Local Folders, I have tried to search for them in my home directory, but found none (find /home/<user name>/ -name <name of a missing Local Folder> -print).

I also wonder whether I could use backup data that were created at the time when I uninstalled whatever version of Thunderbird I had prior to clean installation of Thunderbird 157.0. I recall that uninstallation took a lot of time because a back-up was being created (sudo snap remove thunderbird). I have no idea where that back-up was saved, however.

So now I have Thunderbird 157.0 installed and configured on Ubuntu 26.04, I can send and receive e-mail in all my accounts, but Local Folders created after September 2024 are missing, and the ones that exist contain only relatively old emails (older than September 2024).

I would appreciate help and ideas on how to restore the missing Local Directories and emails from home directory backups.

title: Thunderbird IMAP Aruba: scomparse numerose email da Posta in arrivo e Posta inviata. Le email non sono presenti neppure nella webmail Aruba. Nel profilo esistono file mbox (INBOX e Sent-1) di grandi dimensioni.
creator: paty12082000
content:
Buongiorno,

utilizzo Thunderbird 153.4.0 ESR su Windows 11 con una casella IMAP Aruba (monica@omniaservizifinanziari.com).

Ho riscontrato la scomparsa di una parte consistente delle email sia dalla Posta in arrivo sia dalla Posta inviata.

Le email mancanti non risultano presenti nemmeno nella webmail Aruba.

Ho già effettuato le seguenti verifiche:

account configurato in IMAP; spazio disponibile sulla casella ampiamente sufficiente; riparazione delle cartelle; avvio di Thunderbird in Modalità risoluzione problemi; ricerca globale dei messaggi; verifica delle impostazioni di sincronizzazione e conservazione (nessuna regola di eliminazione attiva);

Nel profilo Thunderbird risultano presenti diverse directory IMAP Aruba:

imaps.aruba.it imaps.aruba-1.it imaps.aruba-2.it

e diversi file mbox di dimensioni significative (INBOX e Sent-1), che fanno pensare alla presenza di dati locali non visualizzati dal programma.

Inoltre il problema si è già verificato in passato sulla stessa casella.

Chiedo cortesemente:

se la presenza delle directory imaps.aruba.it, imaps.aruba-1.it e imaps.aruba-2.it possa indicare profili o sincronizzazioni duplicate; se esistano procedure per verificare il contenuto dei file mbox locali (INBOX, Sent-1, ecc.) e recuperare eventuali messaggi non più visibili; se vi siano controlli specifici da effettuare per verificare una corruzione dell'indice delle cartelle IMAP; se la scomparsa delle email possa dipendere da una sincronizzazione IMAP non corretta o da una ricostruzione del profilo; se possibile chiedere un ripristino anche parziale

Grazie per il supporto

content:
Hello,

I urgently need technical assistance with a serious issue involving Mozilla Thunderbird and my professional certified email account (Aruba PEC, Italy).

I have been using Thunderbird to manage my professional email correspondence for several years.

I organize processed emails into yearly folders (2024, 2025, 2026, etc.), located under my email account in Thunderbird, not under Local Folders.

Today, October 13, 2026, I discovered that all emails dated January through September 2026 have disappeared from my "2026" folder.

Only emails from October 2026 remain.

The missing messages include professional correspondence, certified email delivery receipts, acceptance receipts, and potentially legally significant communications.

What I have verified so far:

The "2026" folder exists both in Thunderbird and in Aruba Webmail.

Both display the same remaining emails from October.

The Trash folder is empty.

The 2024 and 2025 folders still contain their messages.

Thunderbird's retention settings are configured to "Don't delete any messages."

The "2026" folder inherits the account's retention settings.

I did not knowingly delete or move these messages.

Aruba customer support informed me that they cannot restore the missing emails.

I checked Windows Previous Versions and OneDrive, but no backup was found.

I located the local Thunderbird mailbox file named "2026" in the profile's ImapMail directory. It is approximately 3 MB.

Inspection of a copy of this file did not reveal message headers from before October 2026.

I could not find another larger copy of this mailbox file in the Thunderbird profile.

I occasionally remove unused folders under "Local Folders", but I do not recall deleting any folder containing these messages. The affected "2026" folder is located under the IMAP email account.

My questions are:

Could Thunderbird have deleted or moved these messages automatically despite the retention settings?

Could IMAP synchronization, folder corruption, message filters, or compaction explain this situation?

Are there any additional Thunderbird files, caches, databases, or recovery methods worth investigating?

Is there any way to identify when or how the messages were deleted?

What steps should I take to prevent further data loss?

I have preserved a backup copy of my Thunderbird profile and would prefer not to perform potentially destructive operations.

This is particularly serious because the missing messages are part of my professional and legally relevant correspondence.

Any technical guidance would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you very much for your help.

title: Thunderbird 153: fresh profiles become partially unusable after some time; Settings and address autocomplete stop working
creator: d.tsakoev
content:
I was referred here from Thunderbird Bugzilla report 2081665.

We are experiencing a recurring problem with Thunderbird 153 on several Windows workstations in a business environment.

The important point is that the problem also occurs with completely new Thunderbird profiles created from scratch. It is not limited to migrated or old profiles.

On one workstation this has already happened to three separate Thunderbird profiles.

Typical sequence:

1. Thunderbird 153 is installed. 2. A completely new profile is created. 3. Mail accounts are configured manually. 4. Everything initially works normally. 5. After some time the profile begins to malfunction. 6. Thunderbird Settings no longer open/respond. 7. The address books still exist, but address autocomplete when composing a new message stops working. 8. Creating another new profile temporarily fixes the problem, but the same behavior can return later.

Troubleshooting already performed:

- Troubleshoot Mode - extensions disabled - tested without the existing prefs.js - rebuilt Thunderbird caches and profile UI state - recreated indexes/databases - completely removed Thunderbird from Program Files, AppData\Roaming and AppData\Local - clean Thunderbird installation - clean profile created from scratch - Thunderbird executable and profile paths added to Kaspersky Endpoint Security trusted applications/exclusions

Removing prefs.js from an already affected profile did not restore the Settings window.

A clean test profile initially works correctly.

We have also encountered this behavior on other workstations. Some users have more than 100 message filters and many folders, so rebuilding profiles repeatedly causes significant administrative work.

Several affected computers had Windows user accounts renamed in the past.

We also experienced a separate issue where the Attach File dialog stopped appearing while drag-and-drop still worked. Bugzilla identified this as the already known Bug 2077590, so I consider that a separate issue.

For comparison, after completely cleaning Thunderbird from an affected workstation and installing Thunderbird 115.3.1 with a clean profile, the same workstation currently works normally.

Because freshly created Thunderbird 153 profiles can later develop the same problem again, simply recreating the profile does not appear to be a permanent solution.

Environment:

- Windows workstations - Thunderbird 153 ESR - Kaspersky Endpoint Security - multiple IMAP accounts - business environment

What diagnostic information should I collect from the next affected profile before replacing it?

I can provide:

- Thunderbird Troubleshooting Information - Error Console output - profile file names/sizes/timestamps - Windows Event Viewer logs - sanitized prefs.js - comparison with a working fresh profile

Bugzilla report: 2081665 Known separate attachment bug: 2077590

creator: drift2000
content:
Hello,

I would like to understand how to configure Thunderbird with IMAP accounts so that moving messages to Local Folders automatically removes them from the mail server.

I am currently experiencing this issue with Gmail.

1. Manual message moving

When I manually move an email from the Gmail Inbox to a Thunderbird Local Folder, the message is successfully moved locally. However, on the Gmail server, the message remains in the Inbox and is marked as read instead of being deleted.

2. Automatic message filters

I have configured message filters in Thunderbird to automatically move certain incoming emails to Local Folders.

The messages are successfully moved to the specified Local Folders, but instead of being deleted from Gmail, they appear to be archived and remain on the server.

Expected behavior:

- When I manually move an email from an IMAP folder to a Local Folder, it should be removed from the mail server. - When a message filter moves an email to a Local Folder, it should also be removed from the mail server. - Messages moved to Local Folders should retain their original read/unread status.

My questions:

1. How should Thunderbird be configured to achieve this behavior? 2. Are there specific settings for deleting messages from an IMAP server after moving them to Local Folders? 3. Does Gmail require additional IMAP configuration to ensure that moved messages are actually deleted rather than archived? 4. Is there a recommended way to configure message filters for this purpose?

My goal is to use Thunderbird Local Folders for storing emails while removing the original messages from the Gmail server to free up storage space.

Thank you for your help.

title: How to Migrate data from Thunderbird to Outlook?
creator: shivgupta22330
content:
Here is a shorter, more direct breakdown of how to migrate from Thunderbird to Outlook. Because Thunderbird uses MBOX files and Outlook strictly uses PST files, you cannot import the data directly without conversion.

1. The Manual IMAP Method (Free)

• How it works: Use a webmail account (like Gmail) as a bridge. • Steps: 1. Add your IMAP email account to Thunderbird. 2. Drag and drop your Thunderbird emails into a folder under that IMAP account. 3. Add the same email account to Outlook. The emails will sync down automatically.

2. The Drag-and-Drop Method (For small batches)

• Steps: 1. Select your emails in Thunderbird and drag them onto your computer desktop (this saves them as .eml files). 2. Open Outlook and drag those .eml files directly into your Outlook inbox or folder.

title: Why must Thunderbird have a 'Default' email account?
creator: DesertOutlaw1
content:
Example why question is being asked:

Three separate GMX email accounts, each with its own unique password, and NOW Application-specific password for Thunderbird. Aliases are not used or desired. Three different separate accounts that should each have its own outgoing server.

Worked fine until updates to Thunderbird and changes to the GMX server, and Application-specific passwords became a requirement to send and receive email.

Seems like updates to nearly every program and/or app that may be released with the intent to resolve an issue or include a new feature breaks something else. M$ is horrible with updates and labels nearly everything as a critical update so it gets pushed through even when updates are turned off or supposedly permanently disabled by a registry hack; Windows 11 being the absolute worse ever. Why I only have one computer with M$ while all the others are Linux. Problems all the time with M$ while Linux simply continues to work.

Regardless, can setup each GMX account but the default email account name must be used as the user name on the other two GMX accounts on the outgoing server in order to send email. Then the recipient sees the name for the default account rather than the name assigned to the other two accounts, and the Application-specific password for Thunderbird must be changed to that of the default. Then attempting to pull down email for the other two pop accounts comes to a halt, and email messages can only be viewed by going to the online account.

Two separate accounts for yahoo, two for gmail, and one for Charter work fine, each has its own name and outgoing server. Should be the same way for GMX but is not because Thunderbird requires one of the three GMX accounts is set to Default.

Appears by having a Default email account, users are not only restricted by the default account, but email that is sent is done so with he incorrect name, The purpose for three different emails is for email segregation and better management; personal correspondence, business related, and Internet stuff.

Instead of having a 'Default' email account, makes more sense to use a valid email to register Thunderbird after downloading and installing, and then using that email for Support, Boards, assistance, etc. The default email requirement causes too many frustrating unneeded issues that should not occur, along with wasted time, stress and grief. Computers were suppose to make our lives easier and allow us more time for the real world. Biggest lie told since the Bell Labs created the transistor.

content:
Hem Windows masaüstü Thunderbird hem de Thunderbird Android mobil uygulamalarında, uzun süredir sorunsuz kullandığım kişisel e-posta hesabım (to******@live.com) ve test amacıyla yeni oluşturduğum e-posta hesabım (m******s@hotmail.com) üzerinde IMAP bağlantı hatası yaşanmaktadır.

Yaşanan Durum ve Denenen Adımlar: 1. Bu sorun daha önceden var olmayan, sonradan ortaya çıkan bir durumdur. Ayrıca istemcide tanımlı diğer e-posta hesaplarımda hiçbir problem yaşanmazken yalnızca bu iki Microsoft hesabında gözlemlenmektedir. 2. Otomatik ve manuel yapılandırmalarda IMAP (outlook.office365.com:993, SSL/TLS, OAuth 2.0) ve SMTP (smtp-mail.outlook.com:587, STARTTLS, OAuth 2.0) parametreleri eksiksiz girilmektedir. 3. Web tarayıcı yönlendirmesinde Microsoft 2 Adımlı Doğrulama (2FA) ve OAuth 2.0 oturumu başarıyla tamamlanıp izinler verilmektedir. 4. Giriş yapıldıktan hemen sonra istemci "Klasör listesi sunucudan alınamadı - User is authenticated but not connected" hatası döndürmekte ve senkronizasyon başarısız olmaktadır. 5. Sorunun ayarlarla ilgili olup olmadığını doğrulamak adına sıfır açılmış @hotmail.com hesabında IMAP/POP3 erişimleri aktif edilerek deneme yapılmış, aynı hata bu hesapta da tekrarlanmıştır. 6. Söz konusu iki hesap da Android için resmi Microsoft Outlook uygulamasına kurulduğunda ise hiçbir sorun yaşanmadan anında senkronize olmakta ve çalışmaktadır.

Sorunun Thunderbird OAuth 2.0 belirteç (token) işleme mekanizması ile Microsoft IMAP uç noktaları arasındaki el sıkışma uyumsuzluğundan kaynaklandığı değerlendirilmektedir. Konunun incelenmesini rica ederim.

title: Thunderbird keeps freezing after being left idle
creator: pavelconstantinov
content:
• Subject: Severe recurring UI freezes after upgrading Thunderbird from v114 to v150+ — application becomes unresponsive after being left idle**

Hello Thunderbird Support Team,

I'm experiencing a serious and persistent performance issue with Thunderbird that began immediately after upgrading from version 114 to version 150 in September 2026. The problem has continued through multiple subsequent updates and is now severely affecting my daily work.

I've been using Thunderbird for years, and it worked reliably before this major upgrade.

    • The problem**

Thunderbird launches normally and initially works perfectly. However, after I leave it open in the background while working in other applications, it frequently becomes completely unresponsive when I return to it.

Specifically:

- Thunderbird is initially fast and responsive after launching. - After approximately 5–10 minutes, or sometimes after a longer period of inactivity, it begins experiencing severe lag or freezes completely. - When I switch back to Thunderbird, the interface is often unresponsive for several minutes. - I often have to force-close the application through Windows because it becomes practically unusable. - Restarting Thunderbird temporarily restores normal performance, but the problem eventually returns, when it's left idle. - The issue occurs repeatedly throughout the day and makes it very difficult to use Thunderbird reliably.

Importantly, this is not simply slow startup performance. Thunderbird initially works perfectly, and the freezing develops after it has been running for a while, particularly when left in the background.

    • Version and environment**

- Operating system: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit - Thunderbird version before the upgrade: 114 - Version initially upgraded to: 150 - Subsequently confirmed version: 156.0.1 (64-bit), on September 29, 2026 - Problem first appeared: September 2026 - Problem still present: October 22, 2026 - Current Thunderbird version: 158.0.1

    • Troubleshooting already performed**

1. **Global search indexing:** I noticed that Thunderbird's Activity Manager frequently displayed "Indexing messages." I suspected that indexing might be causing the problem.

2. **Disabled Global Search and Indexer (Gloda):** Unfortunately, this made no meaningful difference. Thunderbird continued freezing even with global indexing disabled.

3. **Multiple Thunderbird updates:** The application has been updated repeatedly since the initial upgrade, but the freezing has persisted.

4. **Restarting Thunderbird:** Temporarily resolves the problem, but only until Thunderbird has been running for some time.

    • Additional unusual behavior: Google OAuth authentication**

On at least two occasions, after force-closing an unresponsive Thunderbird process, Google Chrome unexpectedly opened a Google authorization page saying:

"Mozilla Thunderbird Email wants access to your Google Account."

The page also indicated that Thunderbird already had some access to the Google account.

After clicking "Continue," Chrome redirected to a localhost address (127.0.0.1 equivalent, using a dynamically assigned port), which failed with:

"ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — localhost refused to connect."

I suspect this happens because Thunderbird is no longer running to receive the OAuth authorization callback.

I'm not sure whether the Google authorization issue is directly related to the freezes, but the repeated timing is suspicious and could indicate a background synchronization or authentication problem.

    • Impact**

I use Thunderbird extensively for professional correspondence and managing my translation business. These recurring freezes are seriously disrupting my workflow.

The problem has now persisted for over a month, despite updates and troubleshooting. It is becoming increasingly difficult to continue using Thunderbird in this condition.

    • What I would appreciate help investigating**

Could you please advise on how to identify the background process or operation that causes Thunderbird to become unresponsive after it has been running for several minutes?

In particular, I would appreciate guidance on:

- Whether this is a known regression affecting users who upgraded from much older Thunderbird versions. - Whether IMAP synchronization, background authentication, or Google OAuth activity could be responsible. - Whether there are diagnostic logs or performance profiles I can collect while Thunderbird is frozen. - Whether a particular database, profile component, or setting could be responsible without requiring me to rebuild my entire Thunderbird setup. - Whether there are known fixes or workarounds.

I'm happy to provide additional diagnostic information, screenshots, or logs if that would help identify the cause.

I would particularly appreciate a way to capture what Thunderbird is actually doing during these freezes, rather than continuing to try speculative troubleshooting steps.

Thank you in advance for your assistance!

creator: beck4
content:
• Titel: Yahoo-Mail lässt sich in Thunderbird 153.5 unter macOS nicht anmelden – „Es ist ein Problem aufgetreten“**

Hallo zusammen,

ich kann mein Yahoo-Mail-Konto seit etwa zwei Wochen nicht mehr in Thunderbird einrichten. Ich vermute ein Problem mit der Yahoo-OAuth2-Anmeldung.

    • Mein System:**

- Betriebssystem: macOS auf einem MacBook Pro - Thunderbird-Version: 153.5 - Weitere E-Mail-Konten in Thunderbird: Gmail, WEB.DE, GMX und Host Europe. Diese funktionieren alle problemlos.

    • Fehlerbeschreibung:**

Wenn ich mein Yahoo-Konto hinzufügen möchte, öffnet sich das Yahoo-Anmeldefenster. Ich gebe meine vollständige Yahoo-E-Mail-Adresse und mein korrektes Passwort ein. Anschließend erscheint folgende Fehlermeldung:

„Es ist ein Problem aufgetreten. Wir konnten Sie nicht anmelden. Versuchen Sie es bitte auf einem anderen Gerät.“

Darunter befindet sich ein lila Button „Hilfe aufrufen“.

Die Anmeldung bei Yahoo funktioniert dagegen problemlos über Firefox auf demselben Mac mit demselben Passwort. Auch die Anmeldung über meinen Passkey auf dem iPhone funktioniert.

    • Bereits durchgeführte Maßnahmen:**

- Yahoo-Passwort geändert und die Anmeldung über Firefox erfolgreich getestet. - Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung bei Yahoo aktiviert. - Yahoo-Konto in Thunderbird gelöscht und mehrfach versucht, es neu einzurichten. - Authentifizierungsmethode für IMAP und SMTP überprüft: OAuth2. - Cookies und JavaScript in Thunderbird aktiviert. - Im Konfigurationseditor folgende Werte überprüft: 

 - `mailnews.oauth.usePrivateBrowser = true`  - `mailnews.oauth.useExternalBrowser = false`  - `javascript.enabled = true`

- Ein Yahoo-App-Passwort erstellt und versucht, das Konto manuell mit „Passwort, normal“ einzurichten. Thunderbird öffnet trotzdem wieder das Yahoo-Anmeldefenster unter `autodiscover.yahoo.com`, wo dieselbe Fehlermeldung erscheint. - Alte Yahoo-Einträge aus dem Passwortspeicher entfernt. - Doppelte Yahoo-SMTP-Einträge gefunden und den veralteten Eintrag entfernt. - Thunderbird vollständig beendet und neu gestartet.

Nach dem Neustart erscheint teilweise sogar eine Passwortabfrage für `peterbeck127@yahoo.com`, obwohl das Yahoo-Konto nicht mehr in der Kontenliste vorhanden ist.

    • Meine Fragen:**

1. Ist ein bekannter Fehler bei der Yahoo-OAuth2-/PKCE-Anmeldung in Thunderbird 153.5 vorhanden? 2. Warum lehnt Yahoo die Anmeldung in Thunderbird ab, obwohl dieselben Zugangsdaten über Firefox funktionieren? 3. Wie kann ich eventuell verbliebene Yahoo-Anmeldeversuche oder Servereinträge vollständig entfernen, ohne mein Thunderbird-Profil und meine anderen E-Mail-Konten zu beschädigen? 4. Gibt es einen bekannten Workaround oder eine Korrektur für dieses Problem?

Ich möchte mein Yahoo-Konto wieder normal über IMAP und SMTP in Thunderbird verwenden können, ohne meine anderen Konten neu einrichten zu müssen.

Vielen Dank für eure Hilfe!
